'''Dame Linda Partridge''' (born 18 March 1950<ref name="whoswho">{{cite web |url=http://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/article/oupww/whoswho/U30182 |title=PARTRIDGE, Dame Linda |work=Who's Who 2013, A & C Black, an imprint of Bloomsbury Publishing plc, 2013; online edn, Oxford University Press }}{{subscription required}}</ref>) is a British [[geneticist]], who studies the biology and genetics of ageing ([[gerontology|biogerontology]]) and age-related diseases, such as [[Alzheimer's disease]] and [[Parkinson's disease]]. Partridge is currently Weldon Professor of [[Biometry]] at the Institute of Healthy Ageing, Research Department of Genetics, Evolution and Environment, [[University College London]], and the Founding Director Emeritus of the [[Max Planck Institute for the Biology of Ageing]] in Cologne, Germany.{{cn|date=April 2026}}

==Education==
Partridge was educated at the [[Beechwood School, Royal Tunbridge Wells|Convent of the Sacred Heart School]] in [[Tunbridge Wells]]<ref name="thelifescientific">{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b01sm6q6|title=BBC Radio 4 - The Life Scientific, Linda Partridge|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160916003852/http://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b01sm6q6|archive-date=16 September 2016|df=dmy-all}}</ref> and the [[University of Oxford]] from which she was awarded [[Master of Arts]] and [[Doctor of Philosophy]]<ref name="partridgephd">{{cite thesis |degree=DPhil |first=Linda |last=Partridge |title=Behavioural aspects of the ecology of some paridae |publisher=University of Oxford |date=1974 |url=http://solo.bodleian.ox.ac.uk/primo_library/libweb/action/dlDisplay.do?docId=oxfaleph013844925 |author-link=Linda Partridge |url-status=live |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130706193014/http://solo.bodleian.ox.ac.uk/primo_library/libweb/action/dlDisplay.do?docId=oxfaleph013844925 |archive-date=6 July 2013 |df=dmy-all }}</ref> degrees.

== Career ==
After completing her DPhil at the [[University of Oxford]], Partridge became a [[Natural Environment Research Council]] (NERC) post-doctoral fellow at the [[University of York]], and in 1976 moved to the [[University of Edinburgh]] where she became Professor of Evolutionary Biology. In 1994 she moved to [[University College London]] (UCL) as Weldon Professor of Biometry, and was the Director of the Institute of Healthy Ageing between 2007 and 2019. In 2008 Partridge became a Director in the Max Planck Society and the Founding Director of the [[Max Planck Institute for Biology of Ageing]] in Cologne, Germany.<ref>{{Cite web|title=CV|url=https://www.age.mpg.de/science/research-laboratories/partridge/cv|access-date=2020-07-30|website=www.age.mpg.de|language=en-US|archive-date=4 August 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200804193542/https://www.age.mpg.de/science/research-laboratories/partridge/cv/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Awards==
Partridge was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 1996 and appointed [[Order of the British Empire|Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (CBE) in 2003. Her husband, [[Michael J. Morgan]] was also elected FRS in 2005. She was elected to the [[Academy of Medical Sciences]] in 2004,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.acmedsci.ac.uk/p59fid4658.html |title=The Academy of Medical Sciences &#124; Directory of Fellows |access-date=2010-05-13 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110719004800/http://www.acmedsci.ac.uk/p59fid4658.html |archive-date=19 July 2011 }}</ref> and awarded the [[Linnean Society of London]]'s prestigious [[Darwin-Wallace Medal]] in 2008. In 2009, she was appointed [[Dame Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (DBE),<ref>{{London Gazette|issue=59090|date=13 June 2009|page=7|supp=y }}</ref> and received the [[Croonian Lecture]]ship from the [[Royal Society]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://royalsociety.org/Croonian-Lecture |title=The Croonian Lecture (1738) - Prizes - the Royal Society |access-date=2010-05-13 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100521010406/http://royalsociety.org/Croonian-Lecture/ |archive-date=21 May 2010 |df=dmy-all }}</ref>

In March 2009, the [[UKRC]] announced Dame Linda as one of six [[Women of Outstanding Achievement Photographic Exhibition|Women of Outstanding Achievement]] in Science, Engineering and Technology.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ucl.ac.uk/news/news-articles/0903/09031102|title=Professor Linda Partridge: Woman of Outstanding Achievement|website=www.ucl.ac.uk|date=11 March 2009|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121020224409/http://www.ucl.ac.uk/news/news-articles/0903/09031102|archive-date=20 October 2012|df=dmy-all}}</ref>

She was awarded Foreign Honorary Membership of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2010,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.amacad.org/news/new2010.aspx|title=Academy Home - American Academy of Arts & Sciences|website=www.amacad.org|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100423124840/http://www.amacad.org/news/new2010.aspx|archive-date=23 April 2010|df=dmy-all|access-date=13 May 2010}}</ref> and of the German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina in 2023.

She has been awarded Honorary Degrees (DSc) from the [[University of St Andrews]] (2004), the [[University of Oxford]] (2011),<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/10.1093/ww/9780199540884.001.0001/ww-9780199540884-e-30182|title=Partridge, Dame Linda, (born 18 March 1950), Weldon Professor of Biometry, since 1994, and Director, Institute of Healthy Ageing, since 2007, University College London {{!}} WHO'S WHO & WHO WAS WHO|website=www.ukwhoswho.com|language=en|doi=10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.u30182|isbn=978-0-19-954088-4|access-date=2019-01-27}}</ref> the [[University of Bath]] (2011),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.bath.ac.uk/corporate-information/honorary-graduates-2010-to-present/|title=Honorary graduates, 2010 to present|website=University of Bath|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180217192436/http://www.bath.ac.uk/corporate-information/honorary-graduates-2010-to-present/|archive-date=17 February 2018|access-date=13 February 2018|df=dmy-all}}</ref> the [[University of Brighton]] (2012),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.brighton.ac.uk/news/2012/120719honorary_degrees.php |title=Distinguished line-up for honorary degrees - News and events - University of Brighton |access-date=2012-08-09 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120825221521/http://www.brighton.ac.uk/news/2012/120719honorary_degrees.php |archive-date=25 August 2012 }}</ref> the [[University of Kent]] (2017), the [[University of Edinburgh]] (2017), [[Imperial College London]] (2019), and the [[University of East Anglia]] (2019).
